title: `NonConformanceForm.jsx` status dropdown shows all states when editing — no valid-transition guidance; `open → closed` in one click; backend has no NC state machine
description:
Files: `vibrantix-client-panel/src/components/audit-assurance-2/NonConformanceForm.jsx` lines 204–215

Root Cause: The status `<Select>` dropdown renders all possible NC status values (open, in_progress, resolved, verified, closed, cancelled) unconditionally when editing an existing NC. There is no `CAR_VALID_TRANSITIONS`-style map for NCs, neither on the frontend nor in the backend `corrective-action.service.js` NC update path. An auditor can set an NC from `open` directly to `closed` in one save, bypassing the mandatory corrective action and verification lifecycle.

Claude Fix Prompt:
```
Fix D-33 in NonConformanceForm.jsx.

Add a NC_VALID_TRANSITIONS map matching the NC lifecycle:
  open: ['in_progress', 'cancelled']
  in_progress: ['resolved', 'cancelled']
  resolved: ['verified', 'in_progress']
  verified: ['closed']
  closed: []
  cancelled: []

In the status FormControl, filter options to only show valid next states from form.status:
  const validNext = NC_VALID_TRANSITIONS[form.status] || [];
  Render the current status as a read-only badge, then a <Select> showing validNext options only.
  If validNext is empty (closed/cancelled), hide the select and show "No further transitions available."

Also add the same map in corrective-action.service.js (NC update path) and throw AppError.badRequest
if the submitted status is not in NC_VALID_TRANSITIONS[currentNcStatus].
```

title: `ApprovalDrawer.jsx` report governance has no self-approval check — submitter can approve their own report; no independence gate violates ISO 19011 independence principle
description:
Files: `vibrantix-client-panel/src/components/audit-assurance-2/ApprovalDrawer.jsx` lines 82–147, 199–227

Root Cause: `STATE_TO_ACTIONS` maps `in_review → ['approve', 'reject']` with no check that the current user is not the one who submitted the report (transitioned it from `draft → in_review`). The backend `approveReport()` service also does not appear to enforce independence. Any user with report approval access can approve their own report.

Claude Fix Prompt:
```
Fix D-36 in ApprovalDrawer.jsx.

After fetching the governance record, check if the current user submitted the report:
  const currentUserId = useSelector(state => state?.auth?.user?._id);
  const submittedBy = govRecord?.submittedBy;
  const isSelfApproval = submittedBy && currentUserId && submittedBy.toString() === currentUserId.toString();

If isSelfApproval is true and actionKey === 'approve':
  Disable the Approve button and show a warning:
  "You cannot approve a report you submitted. Assign a different reviewer."

Also add a backend check in the report approval service:
  If req.user._id === governanceRecord.submittedBy, throw AppError.forbidden('Self-approval not permitted').
```
